items.title: PyTorch is a hard requirement but is not declared; torch may be pulled from PyPI instead of PyTorchUtils

findings.title: PyTorch is a hard requirement but is not declared; torch may be pulled from PyPI instead of PyTorchUtils
findings.explanation: The extension only declares KonfAI (`set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "KonfAI")`, build_dependencies ["KonfAI"]), while README.md:140-141 tells users to install the SlicerPyTorch extension and states that `impact-reg-konfai` is then pip-installed into Slicer's Python on first open. If `impact-reg-konfai` declares torch in its requirements (its whole purpose is running torch-based presets), pip will pull a PyPI torch build on Impact Reg's first open — exactly the pattern the review policy asks to prevent (torch must come through PyTorchUtils/SlicerPyTorch, declared in build_dependencies and EXTENSION_DEPENDS). I could not read impact-reg-konfai's requirements.txt, so this is flagged as a probable rather than proven path to a duplicated/CUDA-mismatched torch in Slicer's environment.
findings.suggestion: Add PyTorch to EXTENSION_DEPENDS/build_dependencies, and make `impact-reg-konfai` install torch only through PyTorchUtils (or declare torch as an already-satisfied dependency). Point to the exact requirements file in a follow-up message so it can be verified.

items.title: pip-installs impact-reg-konfai (with pinned konfai/konfai-apps) into Slicer's shared Python on every module open

findings.title: pip-installs impact-reg-konfai (with pinned konfai/konfai-apps) into Slicer's shared Python on every module open
findings.explanation: ImpactRegWidget.enter() runs the KonfAI extension's shared `install_package` for a package fetched from PyPI. The author's own comment above the call says that package 'pins and pulls the matching konfai / konfai-apps': if the pin is older than the installed KonfAI extension package, opening Impact Reg can silently downgrade the package another extension depends on, affecting every user of that extension, not only Impact Reg users. The install/prompt behavior lives in the KonfAI extension, which is not in this repository, so whether the user is asked and whether the pin can downgrade KonfAI could not be verified here.
findings.suggestion: State the exact `impact-reg-konfai` version range and confirm on the KonfAI/pip side that its requirements are `>=` (never `==`) for konfai/konfai-apps, that the install is user-confirmed and version-checked, and that a failed install surfaces to the user. If the dependency cannot be relaxed, install it in a dedicated venv instead of Slicer's interpreter, or ship it through the extension build.

findings.title: Module installs or upgrades a pip package into Slicer's shared Python on every open
findings.explanation: enter() calls install_package("impact-reg-konfai", ...) each time the module is opened. Per README.md line 141 and the module's own comment, this pins the matching konfai and konfai-apps versions in Slicer's shared environment. That can change or downgrade packages other extensions use, and I could not confirm from the repository that the user is asked before this happens. The package is needed only for this module, so it is not a safety issue, but the shared-environment side effect needs an explicit, confirmed install.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before installing, and report which konfai/konfai-apps versions will be pinned. Document the environment change in the README. Verify the behaviour of KonfAI's install_package.

items.title: Catalog pins a moving branch and a 9 MB video is committed to the source repo

findings.title: Catalog pins a moving branch and a 9 MB video is committed to the source repo
findings.explanation: scm_revision is "main", so the exact reviewed source can change without a catalog update. The 9 MB tutorial video referenced in the text-scan hints is committed to the repository and is not needed at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a tagged commit for the release, and consider hosting the video externally (the README already links to it).

items.title: Fallback evaluation path can pass None as a CLI argument and crash the run

findings.title: Fallback evaluation path can pass None as a CLI argument and crash the run
findings.explanation: When no evaluation tab is active, `_export_node` can return None (nothing selected in the reference or moving selectors), yet the code unconditionally appends the value to the argument list, so `impact-reg-konfai eval -f None -m None` is constructed or the process launcher raises. The user gets a traceback instead of the 'select a reference image' message; also a failed `slicer.util.saveNode` is ignored and a non-existent filename is forwarded.
findings.suggestion: Check for None (and the boolean return of `saveNode`) and report a clear message with `set_running(False)`, as the registration panel does for missing inputs.

items.title: No automated test despite the CMake test entry

findings.title: No automated test despite the CMake test entry
findings.explanation: `slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)` registers ImpactReg.py as a CTest, but the module file contains no `ScriptedLoadableModuleTest` subclass (only module/widget classes), and the extra Python test is commented out. The registered test can therefore report nothing or fail as 'no test found', and no regression coverage exists for the argument construction that is the heart of the module. The video/tutorial manual workflow is the only validation.
findings.suggestion: Add a ModuleTest class that at least instantiates the widget and, with small synthetic volumes, checks the generated `register`/`eval` argument lists.

findings.title: Unit test registration points at a script with no test class, and the real test is commented out
findings.explanation: ImpactReg/CMakeLists.txt registers ImpactReg.py as a Python unittest under BUILD_TESTING. The file has no unittest class, and the only test file is commented out, so CTest runs no meaningful test. This makes the module's logic (argument construction, output loading) unverified by automated tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that checks the CLI argument construction and the output-loading path with a small fixture, or remove the misleading BUILD_TESTING registration.

items.title: Output file names derive from downloaded app-manifest keys and are joined to the temp folder without sanitization

findings.title: Output file names derive from downloaded app-manifest keys and are joined to the temp folder without sanitization
findings.explanation: The evaluation export uses the manifest key as a filename base: `file_name = self._export_node(selector.currentNode(), key)` and then `self._work_dir / f"{base}.mha"`. Keys come from the preset `app.json` fetched from Hugging Face rather than from this repository, so a manifest containing `../` segments would make `slicer.util.saveNode`/`_write_volume` write outside the temporary folder. Impact is bounded by the fixed `.mha`/`.fcsv` suffixes and requires a compromised or malicious upstream manifest, hence low confidence and minor severity.
findings.suggestion: Whitelist/escape the manifest keys (e.g. take os.path.basename and allow only [A-Za-z0-9_-]) before using them as file names.

items.title: Presets, model weights and a GPU-specific binary are downloaded and executed on first use without per-item confirmation or visible verification

findings.title: Presets, model weights and a GPU-specific binary are downloaded and executed on first use without per-item confirmation or visible verification
findings.evidence: "Registration presets are distributed as KonfAI Apps (downloaded automatically from Hugging Face),"
findings.explanation: The first run of a preset triggers downloads that are executed locally: the preset apps from Hugging Face (`VBoussot/ImpactReg`, whose python/yaml configs drive the run), the TorchScript feature models, `pip install fireants`, and the elastix-IMPACT binary built for the installed CUDA (README.md:103, README.md:141). This is the advertised function and is documented, but nothing in this repository shows hash/signature verification of these payloads; that logic, if any, is in impact-reg-konfai and could not be inspected. A compromised upstream hub repo would therefore run code inside the user's registrations.
findings.suggestion: Surface a confirmation before the first download of each preset/binary and state (in the UI or README) whether downloads are integrity-checked and from which exact repository/revision.

items.title: Registration end callback loads Moved.mha without checking that the file exists

findings.title: Registration end callback loads Moved.mha without checking that the file exists
findings.explanation: Only `Transform.h5` is checked before continuing; `Moved.mha` is read and pushed with no existence test, and per-preset fields are globbed with `sorted((case_dir / "Ensemble").glob("*.h5"))`, which silently yields an empty sequence if `--keep-fields` produced nothing. A partial CLI run therefore raises inside the completion callback (leaving the panel without a message) or leaves an empty DVF sequence behind while the log still reports success.
findings.suggestion: Verify the presence of `Moved.mha` (and warn when `Ensemble/` is empty although uncertainty was ticked) and report the problem through `_update_logs(..., False)`.

items.title: Remote-server access token is passed on the command line (visible in the process list)

findings.title: Remote-server access token is passed on the command line (visible in the process list)
findings.explanation: When a remote server is selected, the login token is appended as a plain CLI argument to the `impact-reg-konfai` process: any local user able to list processes (`ps`) on the same machine can read the credential, and it may also end up in log files or shell history. The same block also chooses the host that receives the fixed/moving images, so the destination is worth documenting explicitly for users.
findings.suggestion: Pass the token through an environment variable or a stdin/temporary file with restrictive permissions instead of argv, and document in the UI that images are uploaded to the chosen host.

findings.title: Remote-server access token is passed on the command line
findings.explanation: When a remote server is selected, the token is appended to the CLI argument list. Command-line arguments are visible to other local users through process listings and may be logged. The data path itself (images sent to a user-chosen server) is opt-in through the server selection.
findings.suggestion: Pass the token through an environment variable or a file with restricted permissions rather than on the command line.

items.title: Terms of downloaded presets and model weights are not stated in the repository

findings.title: Terms of downloaded presets and model weights are not stated in the repository
findings.evidence: FireANTs is distributed under its own license, shipped in each preset's `NOTICE`.
findings.explanation: The module downloads presets, feature models (TotalSegmentator, MIND, anatomix), elastix-IMPACT binaries and fireants at run time. README.md line 103 refers to a NOTICE for FireANTs, but no such file or summary of the terms for the models is in the repository. The redistribution and commercial-use terms for these downloads cannot be checked from the repository alone.
findings.suggestion: Add a short section listing the license of each downloaded model, binary and preset, with links.

items.title: 9 MB tutorial video committed to the repository

findings.title: 9 MB tutorial video committed to the repository
findings.evidence: <!-- Drop Screenshots/SlicerImpactReg-tutorial.mp4 into the README editor on GitHub and paste the user-attachments URL it gives here: GitHub then embeds a player. -->
findings.explanation: The repository carries `Screenshots/SlicerImpactReg-tutorial.mp4` (9 MB) in git history; it is not needed for building or running the module and only bloats the checkout and the archive the index fetches. Non-blocking packaging observation.
findings.suggestion: Host the video on a release asset or external page and link to it, rather than committing it.

findings.title: No research-only / clinical-use disclaimer
findings.evidence: One case: validate the presets on your own data before drawing conclusions from this table.
findings.explanation: The module is positioned for radiotherapy-style CT/CBCT and MR/CT registration and the README reports Dice/TRE improvements on one case, but nothing states that results are research outputs that must be verified before clinical use (README.md:134 only says 'One case: validate the presets on your own data before drawing conclusions from this table'). Users may otherwise treat the automatic transform as clinically validated.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit disclaimer (README and module help/acknowledgment text) that the module is not a certified medical device and that registration results must be checked by a qualified user.
